in-sabellastarte-feather-duster.title: Feather Duster Worm (Sabellastarte)
in-sabellastarte-feather-duster.summary: A tube worm that lives in a tube fixed to rock or sand and spreads a feathery crown to strain food from the water. Easy and reef safe, it pulls in its crown instantly when disturbed.
rows: Crown up to about 6 in (15 cm) across
Filter feeder: fine particle foods and phytoplankton, plus whatever drifts by in a mature tank
Tropical seas; the Atlantic species comes from the Caribbean and Florida, on reefs and rubble
notes: Set the base of the tube in a rock crevice or in the sand.

in-protula-coco-worm.title: Coco Worm (Hard Tube Feather Duster)
in-protula-coco-worm.sci: Protula sp. (sold as P. magnifica or P. bispiralis)
in-protula-coco-worm.summary: A tube worm with a hard, white limestone tube and a bright spiral crown, often growing out of a chunk of coral rock. It needs very clean water and fine foods.
rows: Filter feeder: phytoplankton and fine particle foods
notes: Very sensitive to poor water quality; keep it in a stable, mature tank.
Do not keep it with predatory fish, urchins or serpent stars.
